newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ag attache- Brazil soybean crop 26 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ag attache- Brazil soybean crop 26 mln tonnes.

text.p: An agricultural attache posted at the U.S. embassy in Sao Paolo forecast Brazil's soybean crop at 26 million tonnes in marketing year 1997, unchanged from a previous estimate but below a recent private forecast.

"OAA/Sao Paulo's soybean production forecast for Marketing Year (MY) 1997 (February-January basis) is maintained at 26 million tons which, if achieved, will establish a new Brazilian record," the attache wrote in a report dated Dec 27 which was released in Washington this week.
The forecast is based on 12 million hectares planted and matches the official USDA forecast released Dec 12.

Independent consultant Safras e Mercado estimated late last month that Brazil's 1996/97 soybean crop would reach 26.28 million tonnes and that exports would grow 58 percent to 5.8 million in the 1997/98 marketing year (February/January) from this year's 3.6 million tonnes.
The attache forecast MY 1997 soybean exports at 6 million tonnes and said the volume would be influenced by the lifting of the value-added tax on certain raw material exports including soybeans.
